messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, jordan.blake@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 24 Jun 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Tenor extension & capacity stacking — renewal paperwork coordination

Tom —

Thanks again for the call yesterday. Per our conversation, Veridian is considering extending the contract tenor from 12 months to 18 months to get the price step-down you mentioned, and you also confirmed interest in a capacity-stacking arrangement to cover predictable bursts across quarters.

To move paperwork quickly I attached two starter doc items: Exhibit-C_proposal_v1.docx (proposed tiered capacity and stacking language) and OrderForm_Draft.pdf (covering seats, baseline throughput, and surge blocks). Can you confirm the following so we can hand off to legal?

- Confirm target effective date for the 18-month term (you mentioned Aug 1 as ideal).
- Confirm maximum monthly burst units they want available under stacking (you said ~150k tokens/month burst).
- Any procurement constraints on termination/proration or required contractual language for multi-tranche invoicing?

If you’re good with those, I’ll loop in Marissa (legal liaison) and Jordan (solutions) to propose redlines and a DocuSign-ready order bundle.

Best,

Laura Bennett
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Date: Fri, 26 Jun 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Tenor extension & capacity stacking — renewal paperwork coordination

Laura —

Thanks for the materials. Aug 1 works as the effective date. For stacking, we want an additional 150k tokens/month as you noted, with the ability to convert unused burst capacity into a credit only once per quarter (not monthly). Procurement flagged two items they need clarified before legal:

- Pricing cadence for stacked units (monthly charge vs quarterly true-up).
- Termination proration: our policy requires a pro-rated refund on pre-paid stack blocks if we cancel mid-term (they'll send formal language).

Looping Procurement so they can share their standard clause language. If your legal can accommodate the quarterly credit conversion and a fair proration approach, I think we can move fast.

Tom
Head of CloudOps, Veridian Systems
tom.nguyen@veridian.io
[attachment: Veridian_Procurement_Constraints.pdf (pdf)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 08 Jul 2026 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: redline guidance for tenor extension + stacking (draft)

Laura/Jordan —

I reviewed the attachments and Procurement's note. Below are the redline positions I recommend we propose to Veridian legal (keeps commercial intent but mitigates risk):

1) Term language: Accept 18-month effective Aug 1, include a clear definition of "Renewal Tenor" and tie price step-down schedule to renewal anniversary dates.
2) Capacity stacking: Define "Stacked Units" as non-recurring surge blocks that are billed upfront per quarter, with an optional quarterly true-up. Provide a caps/convertibility clause: unused burst tokens may be converted to service credits once per quarter at a 70% conversion factor.
3) Termination & proration: Standard Redwood position is no refunds for consumed tokens; for pre-paid stacked blocks allow pro rata refund for unused blocks if customer terminates for convenience after 90 days, less a 15% administrative fee. (If customer insists, we can negotiate to 30 days and 25% fee.)
4) Order form: Add Exhibit C as the stacking schedule and include a separate billing line for stacked units to enable Procurement's quarterly reconciliation.
5) SLA / SLO: Add explicit surge SLA language for stacking windows (best-effort plus Xms latency target during stacked periods) and a fallback routing policy to alternate model pool.

I attached a short guidance doc (redline_guidance.docx) with suggested clause snippets. If you want, I can prepare Exhibit-C_v2 with the accepted positions for an external send.

Marissa Cole
Senior Contracts Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
[attachment: redline_guidance.docx (docx)]

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Tenor extension & capacity stacking — renewal paperwork coordination

Tom / Procurement —

Thanks for confirming the Aug 1 effective date. Per Marissa's internal note (quoted below), attached is Exhibit-C_v2 which reflects our proposed commercial/legal balance:

- Stacked Units billed quarterly, with a quarterly true-up option.
- Conversion of unused burst to credits once per quarter at 70% conversion, documented in Exhibit C section 3.
- Termination proration: refund on unused pre-paid stack blocks after 90 days, net of a 15% admin fee (callout included for potential Customer counter-proposal).

Please review Exhibit-C_v2 and highlight any redlines you'd like included. If Procurement can sign off on quarterly billing + true-up, we will prepare an OrderForm final bundle for DocuSign and route to our finance ops for invoice scheduling.

On a timing note: if we can lock language this week we can issue the DocuSign package on Monday 20 Jul and have an executed contract the week of Jul 27.

Thanks — Jordan
